import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import lightgbm as lgb
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# Set working directory and paths
os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) or ".")
input_path = "./input"
submission_path = "./submission"
os.makedirs(submission_path, exist_ok=True)

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(input_path, "train.csv"))
test_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(input_path, "test.csv"))
sample_submission = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(input_path, "sample_submission.csv"))

# Separate features and target
train_X = train_df.drop(columns=["id", "target"])
train_y = train_df["target"]
test_X = test_df.drop(columns=["id"])
test_id = test_df["id"]

# Define categorical and numerical features - ADD f_29 and f_30 as categorical
# These low-cardinality features (2 and 3 unique values) may benefit from categorical encoding
train_X["f_27"] = train_X["f_27"].astype("category")
test_X["f_27"] = test_X["f_27"].astype("category")
train_X["f_29"] = train_X["f_29"].astype("category")
test_X["f_29"] = test_X["f_29"].astype("category")
train_X["f_30"] = train_X["f_30"].astype("category")
test_X["f_30"] = test_X["f_30"].astype("category")

categorical_features = ["f_27", "f_29", "f_30"]
numerical_features = [f for f in train_X.columns if f not in categorical_features]

# Train/validation split (30% validation, stratified)
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    train_X, train_y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=train_y
)

# Prepare training data
train_data = lgb.Dataset(
    X_train, label=y_train, categorical_feature=categorical_features
)
val_data = lgb.Dataset(
    X_val, label=y_val, categorical_feature=categorical_features, reference=train_data
)

# Train LightGBM model with same parameters as previous solution
params = {
    "objective": "binary",
    "metric": "auc",
    "boosting_type": "gbdt",
    "num_leaves": 31,
    "learning_rate": 0.05,
    "feature_fraction": 0.9,
    "bagging_fraction": 0.8,
    "bagging_freq": 5,
    "verbose": -1,
    "seed": 42,
    "force_col_wise": True,
}

model = lgb.train(
    params,
    train_data,
    num_boost_round=500,
    valid_sets=[val_data],
    valid_names=["valid"],
    callbacks=[
        lgb.early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50, verbose=False),
        lgb.log_evaluation(period=0),
    ],
)

# Validate on hold-out set
y_val_pred = model.predict(X_val)
val_auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, y_val_pred)
print(f"Validation AUC-ROC: {val_auc:.6f}")

# Predict on test set
test_predictions = model.predict(test_X)

# Create submission file
submission_df = pd.DataFrame({"id": test_id, "target": test_predictions})
submission_df.to_csv(os.path.join(submission_path, "submission.csv"), index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to {submission_path}/submission.csv")
print(f"Submission shape: {submission_df.shape}")
print(f"Submission head:\n{submission_df.head()}")
plan: I propose to improve the model's feature representation by treating the low-cardinality integer features `f_29` and `f_30` as categorical features alongside `f_27`. These features have only 2 and 3 unique values respectively, so treating them as categorical may capture different interaction patterns that numerical encoding misses. I will keep all other parameters identical to the previous solution (num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05, etc.) to ensure this is a single atomic change that can be experimentally evaluated.
